findings.title: Rate-limit bucket key drops userId, collapsing per-user buckets into per-route buckets

steps.to: rate-limit bucket identity used by callers
steps.relationship: the returned string is the bucket key, now identical for every user on a route

impactPath.limitation: Callers of the exported rateBucket function are not present in the supplied context; propagation to the rate limiter is inferred from the function name, its userId/route parameters, and the previous key format.

findings.behavioralContract: Rate-limit bucket keys are scoped per user and per route, so each identity has an independent quota for a route.
findings.failureScenario: All users hitting the same route now map to one bucket: traffic from a single identity (or a burst of legitimate users) exhausts the shared quota and throttles everyone on that route, or conversely a per-user cap is enforced only globally, weakening abuse containment.
findings.reachability: rateBucket is an exported function and its return value directly encodes the bucket identity, so every caller that keys limits on this value reaches the collapsed keying immediately.
findings.rootCause: The head change removes userId from the returned key while keeping userId in the signature, leaving it unused and changing the key namespace from per-user-per-route to per-route.
findings.impact: Per-user rate-limit isolation is lost; one identity's consumption affects the limits of all identities on the same route.
findings.blastRadius: Every caller of rateBucket and all users of routes rate-limited with this key.
assumptions: Callers use the returned string as a rate-limit bucket key, as the function name and prior implementation indicate.
counterEvidence: The change could be intentional if the product now wants a single global per-route limit; however, the unchanged signature and retained unused userId parameter provide no supporting evidence for that intent.
findings.uncertainty: Caller usage is not in the supplied context, so the concrete rate limiter behavior affected cannot be confirmed from this file alone.
findings.fix: Restore the composite key: return `${userId}:${route}`;. If a global per-route limit is actually intended, instead remove the unused userId parameter and update the function name/callers to make the new contract explicit.
findings.regressionTest: Add a unit test asserting rateBucket('alice','/api') !== rateBucket('bob','/api'); before the fix both calls return the identical string, after the fix they differ.

findings.title: rateBucket drops userId from the bucket key, merging per-user rate buckets per route

steps.from: rateBucket(userId, route) return value in src/bucket.ts
steps.relationship: the returned key is consumed by the throttle caller, which still passes userId expecting it to scope the bucket

impactPath.limitation: The limiter state keyed by the returned identifier downstream of gateway.throttle is outside the supplied context.

findings.behavioralContract: A rate bucket key must uniquely identify the limiting scope; per-user limiting requires the key to incorporate userId.
findings.failureScenario: Two users call the same route through gateway.throttle. Both receive the identical key 'route' instead of 'userId:route', so they share one bucket: a high-volume user exhausts the budget and other users on that route are throttled, or per-user limits are no longer enforced independently.
findings.reachability: Every call path through gateway.throttle passes userId and route; the head implementation ignores userId for all of them.
findings.rootCause: The head change returns route alone, dropping the `${userId}:` prefix from the composed bucket key.
findings.impact: Per-user rate limiting collapses to per-route shared limiting, causing cross-user quota interference.
findings.blastRadius: All callers of rateBucket — at minimum gateway.throttle and every user/route pair routed through it.
assumptions: The return value of rateBucket is used as the rate-limit bucket key, consistent with its name and the throttle caller
No documented migration to per-route limiting accompanies this change
counterEvidence: If per-route limiting was intentionally adopted, the remaining unused userId parameter and unchanged caller would still make this an inconsistent, incomplete change
findings.uncertainty: The downstream limiter implementation is not in the supplied context, so the exact throttle semantics of the merged bucket are inferred from naming and the caller.
findings.fix: Restore the composite key `${userId}:${route}`; if per-route limiting is intended, remove the userId parameter and update all callers and keying consumers together.
findings.regressionTest: Assert rateBucket('u1', '/a') !== rateBucket('u2', '/a') (and that each incorporates its userId). Before the fix both return '/a' and the test fails; after the fix it passes.
